title: Widen the model: dim 512 -> 640 at depth 12
description: ASPECT_RATIO 40 -> 48, so model_dim 512 -> 640 with 5 heads of 128; depth, batch, LR constants untouched.
reflection: NEGATIVE/wash: val_bpb 0.986933 vs baseline 0.986277 (+0.00066, inside the ~0.0009 noise floor). Numbers: 100.9M params (was 71.3M), FLOPs/token 5.03e8 (was 3.46e8, +45%), total_tokens 246.0M (was 331.5M, -26%), num_steps 1877, steady-state MFU 41.5% (was 38.5%), peak VRAM 40.7GB (was 32.1GB). Read: width at fixed compute pays for itself almost exactly -- 41% more parameters bought back the 26% token loss and no more. Combined with depth's decay (8->10 -0.0082, 10->12 -0.0027), the capacity axis is now essentially exhausted at this 5-minute budget: the model is at or near compute-optimal shape, both in size and in aspect ratio. Further scaling in either direction should not be bought. Remaining runs are better spent on structure that changes quality per FLOP rather than capacity: MLP expansion ratio, window pattern, or the untested schedule constants (WARMDOWN_RATIO). MFU did keep rising (38.5 -> 41.5%) with width, so if anyone does revisit capacity, width is the cheaper direction of the two, but it is still not a win.
